create.name: Jonathan Foust
create.bio:
Jonathan Foust grew up on a Pennsylvania farm in a Quaker family and first met meditation and yoga at boarding school. After teaching in Niger with the Peace Corps he arrived at the Kripalu ashram in his mid-twenties and stayed for twenty-four years, practising and teaching yoga and meditation, leading groups, and later helping to turn Kripalu into a non-sectarian retreat centre, which he served as president. He then moved to the Washington, DC area, where he lives with his wife, the meditation teacher Tara Brach.

He serves as one of the guiding teachers at the Insight Meditation Community of Washington, and he co-founded the Meditation Teacher Training Institute. His own approach, which he calls Body-Centered Inquiry, combines insight meditation with attention to the body's felt sense, drawing on Eugene Gendlin's Focusing. Each Monday evening he gives a free webcast of guided meditation and a dharma talk, and hundreds of his talks and meditations are available on his podcast and YouTube channel. He also leads daylong and residential retreats, co-teaches week-long silent vipassana retreats, and runs the Year of Living Mindfully, a year-long programme of daily practice, retreats and community support.

courses.title: A Year of Living Mindfully
courses.description: A year-long programme that starts each September, combining a daily meditation commitment, retreats, study, somatic inquiry practice and a supportive peer group. Tuition is on three tiers.

courses.title: Retreats and Workshops
courses.description: Daylong retreats in the Washington, DC area, week-long silent vipassana retreats he co-leads three times a year, and a five-day Kripalu programme joining meditation with Focusing and intuition.

free_resources.title: Monday Night Meditation Webcast
free_resources.description: A free weekly livestream with a guided meditation and a dharma talk, offered on donation and later posted as audio and video.

free_resources.title: Talks and Meditations
free_resources.description: His archive of recorded dharma talks, guided meditations and short writings, free to stream.
